name: transmigration of souls (metempsychosis)

attributes.attribute: a belief that the soul moves into other bodies
recorded in some texts from Roman times
changed into a fly and impregnated her own mother
lived as an eagle and as a salmon

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Transmigration of souls is a cosmological concept. Teachers of the past do not agree on one point. Did the ancient Celts hold a faith in a return after death? Some writings from Roman times seem to record such a belief. Those who accept the idea hold that humans were not always reborn as humans. Instead the soul moved into the bodies of animals, birds, and even insects. Irish mythology is full of such changes. The fair Etain was turned into a fly and so impregnated her own mother. Friuch and Rucht, the two quarrelsome swineherds, came back as ravens, stags, and bulls. The bard Tuan mac Cairill lived as an eagle and as a salmon.

okr.objective: Record the Celtic belief in the transmigration of souls.
key_results: Scholars disagree about the Celtic belief in reincarnation
Some Roman-era texts appear to record the belief
The soul could move into animals, birds, and insects
